newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end shade lower in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end shade lower in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Bombay shares closed slightly lower on Thursday, in a session that lacked any major activity, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) finished 13.29 points, or 0.43 percent, lower at a provisional 3,112.77 off 3,134.14.
"The market seems to be in a state of inertia....there is hardly any major activity," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive at Lloyds Finance, a local brokerage.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index fell 9.42 points, or 1.05 percent, to end at a provisional 887.58.
ITC closed 0.50 rupees lower at 263.50 at the BSE after rising to 271.0 in mid-session, with 2.59 million shares traded.
Indian financial institutions and B.A.T Industries Plc, major shareholders of ITC, will review operations of the tobacco giant at a board meeting on Friday.
Last month, a federal agency arrested several senior ITC officials including two former chairmen for allegedly violating India's foreign exchange rules.
On Tuesday, an Indian court rejected the bail plea of the two former chairmen and remanded them to judicial custody until November 26.
Foreign funds were bidders in pivotals including BHEL, Indian Hotels, Hindustan Lever, Wartsila Diesels and Gujarat Ambuja Cements, traders said.
"There has been some fund buying...but I would classify it as isolated buying," Lloyds' Agarwal said.
SBI lost 2.75 rupees to 220.0 rupees, TISCO 1.75 to 166.75, Reliance 1.25 to 184.25, ACC 40.70 to 1,365.0, TELCO 9.75 to 406.75 and Bajaj Auto 3.25 to 942.0.
Hind Lever gained 10.70 to 805.0, Indian Hotels 14.7 to 670.0 and BHEL 2.50 to 185.75.
